prompt: A logo is shrunk by a dilation centered at the origin with scale factor $\frac{1}{2}$. One corner of the logo is at $(6, -4)$. Write the coordinates of that corner after the dilation, in the form (x, y).
hint: A dilation centered at the origin multiplies BOTH coordinates by the scale factor.

hints.text: A dilation centered at the origin multiplies BOTH coordinates by the scale factor.

explanation: For a dilation centered at the origin, $(x, y) \to (kx, ky)$.
The image corner is $(3, -2)$ — the same direction from the origin, half as far out.

alternativeExplanations.title: Shape stays, size changes
steps: A dilation is the only one of these four transformations that changes size; translations, reflections and rotations keep it.
Scale factor less than $1$ shrinks the logo toward the origin, so both coordinates get smaller in absolute value — but the negative stays negative.
